title: Inodes and links
subtitle: Names vs inodes — flip for meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: File-system object ID: metadata, owner/perms, and disk block locations — not the name
cards.notes: Names live in directories; inode = ID card + map of data blocks

cards.meaning: List of names assigned to inodes (., .., and each child)
cards.notes: Phone book of names → inode numbers

cards.meaning: How many directory entries point at an inode; data deletable when count is 0 and nothing has it open
Direct pointer to an inode — another name for the same file
Create a hard link (extra name for the same inode)
Hard links cannot cross file systems (inodes unique per FS)
cards.notes: Cannot hard-link from disk A to a file on separately mounted disk B

cards.meaning: Pointer to a path/file name, not to the inode
cards.notes: Its own inode, type symlink; can dangle

cards.meaning: Soft link usually becomes invalid (dangling); hard link still works
cards.notes: Hard = same inode; soft = sticky note with a path

cards.meaning: Hard link: data remains if link count > 0. Soft link: link breaks; original gone
cards.notes: Deleting the soft link itself does not delete the original

cards.meaning: Allowed — soft links can cross file systems; hard links cannot
List with inode numbers; same number = hard links to the same file
